drugs.name: Methotrexate (Rheumatrex/Trexall)
drugs.mechanism: Folate antagonist inhibiting dihydrofolate reductase and AICAR transformylase, leading to adenosine accumulation with anti-inflammatory effects on T cells and neutrophils
drugs.approval: FDA approved 1972 (RA). First-line DMARD. ACR/EULAR anchor drug.
drugs.efficacy: ACR20 response ~50-65% as monotherapy at 6 months; superior when combined with biologics

drugs.name: Adalimumab (Humira)
drugs.mechanism: Fully human anti-TNF monoclonal antibody that binds soluble and membrane-bound TNF, blocking TNFR1/TNFR2 signaling and reducing synovial inflammation
drugs.approval: FDA approved 2002 (RA). Most prescribed biologic globally.
drugs.efficacy: ACR20 ~60% at 6 months; inhibits radiographic progression by ~50% at 1 year

drugs.name: Etanercept (Enbrel)
drugs.mechanism: Soluble TNFR2-Fc fusion protein that acts as a decoy receptor, neutralizing both TNF-alpha and lymphotoxin-alpha
drugs.approval: FDA approved 1998 (RA). First approved anti-TNF biologic.
drugs.efficacy: ACR20 ~59% at 6 months; comparable to adalimumab in head-to-head trials

drugs.name: Infliximab (Remicade)
drugs.mechanism: Chimeric mouse-human anti-TNF monoclonal antibody; binds both soluble and membrane-bound TNF, inducing apoptosis of TNF-expressing cells
drugs.approval: FDA approved 1999 (RA). Must be combined with methotrexate.
drugs.route: IV infusion at weeks 0, 2, 6, then every 8 weeks
drugs.efficacy: ACR20 ~50% at 30 weeks with MTX; significantly inhibits joint destruction

drugs.name: Certolizumab Pegol (Cimzia)
drugs.mechanism: PEGylated humanized anti-TNF Fab fragment (no Fc region); neutralizes TNF without inducing complement or ADCC cytotoxicity
drugs.approval: FDA approved 2009 (RA). Can be used in pregnancy (minimal placental transfer).
drugs.efficacy: ACR20 ~58% at 24 weeks with MTX; rapid onset (1-2 weeks)

drugs.name: Golimumab (Simponi)
drugs.mechanism: Fully human anti-TNF monoclonal antibody with high affinity; neutralizes both soluble and transmembrane TNF
drugs.approval: FDA approved 2009 (RA, PsA, AS). Monthly dosing convenience.
drugs.efficacy: ACR20 ~55% at 14 weeks with MTX; sustained efficacy through 5 years

drugs.name: Tocilizumab (Actemra)
drugs.mechanism: Humanized anti-IL-6R monoclonal antibody blocking both membrane-bound and soluble IL-6R, inhibiting IL-6-mediated JAK1/JAK2-STAT3 signaling
drugs.approval: FDA approved 2010 (RA). Superior to adalimumab in monotherapy (ADACTA trial).
drugs.route: IV infusion every 4 weeks or subcutaneous weekly
drugs.efficacy: ACR20 ~70% at 24 weeks; monotherapy superior to MTX and adalimumab

drugs.name: Sarilumab (Kevzara)
drugs.mechanism: Fully human anti-IL-6Rα monoclonal antibody; higher affinity for IL-6R than tocilizumab
drugs.approval: FDA approved 2017 (RA). Fully human antibody reduces immunogenicity risk.
drugs.efficacy: ACR20 ~58-66% at 24 weeks with MTX; comparable to tocilizumab

drugs.name: Tofacitinib (Xeljanz)
drugs.mechanism: Oral JAK inhibitor preferentially targeting JAK1 and JAK3; blocks signaling downstream of IL-2, IL-4, IL-7, IL-9, IL-15, IL-21, and type I IFN receptors
drugs.approval: FDA approved 2012 (RA). First-in-class JAK inhibitor.
drugs.route: Oral, twice daily (or XR once daily)
drugs.efficacy: ACR20 ~60% at 3 months; non-inferior to adalimumab (ORAL Strategy)

drugs.name: Baricitinib (Olumiant)
drugs.mechanism: Oral selective JAK1/JAK2 inhibitor; blocks signaling downstream of IL-6, type I IFN, IFN-gamma, and GM-CSF receptors
drugs.approval: FDA approved 2018 (RA). Superior to adalimumab in RA-BEAM trial.
drugs.efficacy: ACR20 ~70% at 12 weeks; superior to adalimumab for ACR20 and DAS28-CRP improvement

drugs.name: Upadacitinib (Rinvoq)
drugs.mechanism: Oral selective JAK1 inhibitor; engineered for JAK1 selectivity over JAK2/JAK3/TYK2 to minimize hematologic adverse effects
drugs.approval: FDA approved 2019 (RA). JAK1 selectivity profile.
drugs.efficacy: ACR20 ~71% at 12 weeks with MTX; superior to adalimumab in SELECT-COMPARE

drugs.name: Rituximab (Rituxan)
drugs.mechanism: Chimeric anti-CD20 monoclonal antibody depleting B cells via ADCC, CDC, and apoptosis induction
drugs.approval: FDA approved 2006 (RA after TNF failure). Not first-line; used in seropositive RA.
drugs.route: IV infusion, 2 doses 2 weeks apart, repeated every 6-12 months
drugs.efficacy: ACR20 ~54% at 24 weeks in TNF-inadequate responders (REFLEX trial); best response in RF/anti-CCP positive patients

drugs.name: Abatacept (Orencia)
drugs.mechanism: CTLA4-Ig fusion protein that binds CD80/CD86 on APCs, blocking CD28-mediated T cell costimulation and reducing T cell activation
drugs.approval: FDA approved 2005 (RA). Only approved T cell costimulation blocker.
drugs.route: IV infusion monthly or subcutaneous weekly
drugs.efficacy: ACR20 ~65% at 6 months with MTX; unique T-cell targeted mechanism

drugs.name: Hydroxychloroquine (Plaquenil)
drugs.mechanism: Inhibits endosomal acidification, blocking TLR7/9 activation; reduces antigen presentation and cytokine production
drugs.approval: FDA approved 1955. Mild DMARD used in combination therapy for mild-moderate RA.
drugs.efficacy: ACR20 ~30-40% as monotherapy; modest effect on radiographic progression; primarily used as adjunct therapy

drugs.name: Leflunomide (Arava)
drugs.mechanism: Inhibits de novo pyrimidine synthesis by blocking DHODH, selectively reducing activated T lymphocyte proliferation
drugs.approval: FDA approved 1998 (RA). Alternative first-line DMARD to methotrexate.
drugs.efficacy: ACR20 ~52% at 12 months; comparable to methotrexate and sulfasalazine

drugs.name: Sulfasalazine (Azulfidine)
drugs.mechanism: Prodrug cleaved by gut bacteria into 5-ASA and sulfapyridine; inhibits NF-κB, reduces inflammatory cytokine production, and scavenges reactive oxygen species
drugs.approval: FDA approved 1950. Part of triple therapy (MTX+SSZ+HCQ).
drugs.efficacy: ACR20 ~40-50%; triple therapy (MTX+SSZ+HCQ) non-inferior to etanercept+MTX (TEAR trial)

drugs.name: Anakinra (Kineret)
drugs.mechanism: Recombinant IL-1 receptor antagonist (IL-1Ra); competitively blocks IL-1α and IL-1β binding to IL-1R1
drugs.approval: FDA approved 2001 (RA). Limited use due to daily injections and modest efficacy vs TNF inhibitors.
drugs.efficacy: ACR20 ~38% at 24 weeks; more effective in systemic JIA and autoinflammatory diseases than RA

drugs.name: Prednisone
drugs.mechanism: Glucocorticoid binding to cytoplasmic GR leads to nuclear translocation, transrepression of pro-inflammatory genes (AP-1, NF-κB), and transactivation of anti-inflammatory genes (annexin-1, IL-10)
drugs.approval: Standard of care for rapid symptom control. Bridge therapy while DMARDs take effect.
drugs.route: Oral, daily (tapered to lowest effective dose)
drugs.efficacy: Rapid symptomatic relief within days; inhibits radiographic progression at low doses (≤7.5mg/day)

drugs.name: Cyclosporine (Neoral/Sandimmune)
drugs.mechanism: Calcineurin inhibitor forming complex with cyclophilin to block NFAT dephosphorylation, inhibiting IL-2 transcription and T cell activation
drugs.approval: Used off-label for refractory RA. Limited by nephrotoxicity.
drugs.efficacy: Modest efficacy in RA; ACR20 ~40% in methotrexate-resistant patients; rarely used now due to biologics availability

drugs.name: Denosumab (Prolia/Xgeva)
drugs.mechanism: Fully human anti-RANKL monoclonal antibody; inhibits osteoclast differentiation and activation by blocking RANK-RANKL interaction
drugs.approval: FDA approved 2010 (osteoporosis). Used in RA to prevent bone erosion and glucocorticoid-induced osteoporosis.
drugs.efficacy: Reduces bone erosion progression in RA by ~35% at 12 months (DESIRABLE trial); does not reduce synovial inflammation

drugs.name: Mycophenolate Mofetil (CellCept)
drugs.mechanism: Inhibits de novo purine synthesis, selectively suppressing T and B lymphocyte proliferation
drugs.approval: Used off-label for refractory RA and RA-ILD (interstitial lung disease). Limited efficacy data.
drugs.efficacy: Modest efficacy in refractory RA; ACR20 ~30-40% in small studies; primarily used for RA-associated ILD

drugs.name: Azathioprine (Imuran)
drugs.mechanism: Prodrug converted to 6-mercaptopurine, which incorporates into DNA as thioguanine nucleotides, inhibiting purine synthesis and lymphocyte proliferation
drugs.approval: Used off-label for refractory RA. Largely replaced by MTX and biologics.
drugs.efficacy: ACR20 ~35-45% in MTX-inadequate responders; limited by GI and hematologic toxicity

drugs.name: Filgotinib (Jyseleca)
drugs.mechanism: Oral selective JAK1 inhibitor with 30-fold selectivity over JAK2; blocks IL-6, type I/II IFN, and common gamma chain cytokine signaling
drugs.approval: Approved in EU/Japan 2020 (RA). Not FDA approved (pending). JAK1 selectivity profile.
drugs.efficacy: ACR20 ~66-77% at 12-24 weeks in FINCH trials; comparable to adalimumab

drugs.name: Ozoralizumab (Nanozora)
drugs.mechanism: Bispecific anti-TNF/anti-HSA nanobody (VHH); engineered for extended half-life via albumin binding and enhanced tissue penetration due to small size (38 kDa vs 150 kDa IgG)
drugs.approval: Approved in Japan 2022 (RA). First nanobody approved for RA.
drugs.efficacy: ACR20 ~60-70% at 16 weeks with MTX; non-inferior to conventional anti-TNF mAbs in Japanese trials
